The core insight centers on the tension between truth and consistency in cognition. Initially, truth-seeking involves apparent contradictions—such as those in quantum mechanics and relativity—which reflect incomplete understanding. Over time, these inconsistencies resolve into coherent frameworks. This process mirrors the dialectical progression from thesis to antithesis to synthesis, as seen in Hegelian philosophy and Marxist thought. The failure mode arises when institutions enforce premature consistency, suppressing dissenting voices and halting epistemic development. Psychological conformity acts as a barrier, where individuals avoid deviation due to fear of social ostracism. This leads to institutionalized rigidity, akin to how rigid control systems lose adaptability. The epistemic lens reveals that true progress requires embracing contradiction until resolution, while GSI models this through Bayesian updating with adaptive priors. GSE maps this as a dynamic state-space problem where deviation triggers feedback loops that either reinforce or suppress novelty.
